properties.name: The near-match refusal asks about relatedness, not only duplication
properties.rationale:
A′, from `dec:idea-governance-rides-the-tool-that-does-the-thing`, built on `Decision.kind` (#393).

THE INSIGHT IT RESTS ON: the refusal ALREADY FIRES and already makes the caller read the near-matches — for DUPLICATION. It then throws that reading away for RELATEDNESS. They are already looking at the list; they were only ever asked half a question about it. So no new interruption is added; an existing one asks one more thing.

MEASURED 2026-08-30: 140 of 207 ideas carry a relation and `no_relation_note` had been used TWICE, so for the 67 unlinked ideas "nobody looked" and "looked and found nothing" are indistinguishable — the distinction the field exists to preserve.

⚠️ SCOPED TO `exploratory`, AND ONLY WHEN NEAR-MATCHES EXIST. Unscoped it would land on the Requirement/Capability/ChangeEvent capture path Alex's 2026-08-30 report names as his existing friction, and an idea nothing resembles is asked nothing at all. That scoping is why `Decision.kind` had to exist first.

🛑 IT COMPELS A RECORDED JUDGEMENT, NEVER AN EDGE. The refusal names the fabrication hazard where the pressure to fabricate is — a false neighbour is worse than a missing one, because anything searching by neighbourhood repeats it forever — and states that the note is a full answer rather than the weaker one.

⚠️ IT ONLY REACHES NEW IDEAS. The 207 already in the graph carry no `kind`, deliberately (backfilling would launder the id prefix being retired into a property), so A′ is silent on them.
properties.subject: system
properties.summary: `add_decision` gains `related_to` (reusing `RelationLinkReq`, the shape `review_relations` already takes) and `no_relation_note`. When the Decision is `kind: exploratory` AND the duplicate guard surfaced near-matches, the caller must answer the RELATEDNESS question as well as the sameness one — either drawing the relations they judged real, each with its evidence, or recording what they looked at and why none was honestly related. Both land in the SAME call via core's `review_relations`, so the judgement cannot be lost between two. Five tests. A test caught a real defect in the first cut: the reply was built BEFORE the note was written, so a caller following "read the result back" would have been told the judgement was not recorded when it was — the same unreadable-success shape a consumer's field report is about. Fixed by re-reading after the review.
